Finding.0: Guests are mostly positive in their own words, but a distinct negative minority exists.
Finding.1: Amenity sentiment differs: Breakfast is discussed most positively and Air conditioning least positively (amenities with >=100 mentions; smaller samples are not ranked).
Finding.2: Staff and service are mentioned very often and mostly positively, yet staff behaviour and slow service are leading specific complaints.
Finding.3: Cleanliness/hygiene is the most frequent specific complaint, and bathroom, bedding and AC themes are over-represented in negative reviews.
Finding.4: Food and breakfast are broadly in line with the corpus average and mostly positive.
Finding.5: Price and value-for-money comments are more negative than the corpus average.
Finding.6: Ratings alone hide reasons, and many reviews are very short.

Evidence.0: VADER: 76.3% positive / 5.1% neutral / 18.6% negative; rating-based reference: 73.8% / 4.9% / 21.3%.
Evidence.1: Net sentiment of sentences: Breakfast +55.0 pp (1754 mentions); Air conditioning +0.0 pp (954 mentions). Reviews of hotels listing Fitness / gym have a rating-positive share +8.8 pp higher than hotels not listing it when compared within the same hotel category (raw difference +11.0 pp).
Evidence.2: Staff: 77.9% positive / 20.8% negative among 8,506 mentions; Service: 79.0% / 19.6% among 6,916. Negative reviews cite rude/unhelpful staff 992 times and slow/poor service 570 times.
Evidence.3: 1,497 negative reviews (30.7%) contain a cleanliness complaint. Share of negative reviews among mentions: Bathroom 52.0%; Bed / bedding 55.7%; Air conditioning 50.8% (overall 18.6%).
Evidence.4: Whole-review sentiment of reviews mentioning breakfast (1,754): 79.3% positive / 19.0% negative; food: 82.9% / 15.0% vs 76.3% / 18.6% overall; 345 negative reviews describe a food/breakfast quality problem.
Evidence.5: 3,565 reviews mention price/value: 29.9% negative vs 18.6% overall. 576 negative reviews cite overpricing/charges.
Evidence.6: 22.3% of rating-negative reviews are not labelled negative by their text; 25.2% of reviews have <=5 words; hotel-level mean VADER compound vs customer_rating Spearman = 0.64.

Business implication.0: Track the share of negative reviews (not just the average rating); the negative minority is where concrete problems are described.
Business implication.1: Amenities associated with more positive text deserve priority in positioning; amenities that are frequently mentioned alongside complaints need reliability checks (association, not proven cause).
Business implication.2: Staff conduct and responsiveness are controllable: training and a complaint-response routine can protect a strength.
Business implication.3: Prioritise housekeeping standards and a maintenance checklist (bathroom fittings, hot water, bedding, AC) - areas where a failure is explicitly described.
Business implication.4: Maintain quality; monitor the minority complaints.
Business implication.5: Align price with visible quality and communicate charges clearly; value complaints often travel with room-quality complaints.
Business implication.6: Combine rating and text signals, prompt guests for specifics, and respond to negative reviews that describe concrete problems.

recs: **Fix hygiene first.** Cleanliness/hygiene is the most frequent complaint (1,497 negative reviews, 30.7%). Introduce daily room/bathroom inspection checklists and follow up on any review that mentions dirt, smell or pests.

**Run preventive maintenance on bathrooms, bedding and AC.** Bathroom reviews are 52.0% negative; Bed / bedding reviews are 55.7% negative; Air conditioning reviews are 50.8% negative versus 18.6% overall - these are fixable equipment/linen issues.

**Invest in staff conduct and responsiveness.** Rude/unhelpful staff appears in 992 negative reviews and slow/poor service in 570. Add service-recovery training and a response-time target for complaints.

**Prioritise and quality-check amenities.** Fitness / gym and similar amenities are associated with a higher rating-positive share (+8.8 pp within the same hotel category, raw +11.0 pp); amenities such as Air conditioning are often mentioned in complaints (net +0.0 pp), so guarantee they work reliably rather than just listing them.

**Use review sentiment as an early-warning indicator.** VADER's compound score separates 1-2 star from 4-5 star reviews well (ROC-AUC 0.95); alert managers when a hotel's share of negative reviews rises, and monitor the top pain-point counts monthly.

**Combine text sentiment with the hotel-success model.** Hotel-level mean sentiment is positively related to the hotel's rating (Spearman 0.64). Because success was defined from rating, use sentiment and pain points as *diagnostic* features beside Review 1's predictors, validated on a proper train/test split, rather than as extra predictors of the same label.
**Benchmark within hotel category.** Negative-text share ranges from 7.6% (5-star hotel) to 24.0% (2-star hotel); compare a hotel with peers of the same category rather than the overall average.

**Collect richer feedback.** 25.2% of reviews are 5 words or fewer and neutral (3-star) reviews are hardest to interpret (VADER F1 0.14); use short guided prompts (e.g. room, staff, value) to capture usable detail.
